items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Sonny Terry, who was my neighbor. I used to hit home runs, whiffle ball into his yard.

ctx.x: But it was cool with me but it wasn’t cool. And so if you wanted to go to Folk City to see a blues act, because they had blues acts, like Sonny Terry, who was my neighbor. I used to hit home runs, whiffle ball into his yard. I think he lived at the corner of Keno and Pompey in Hollis. And we didn’t want to hear this unknown folk singer do his thing, so you booed him to make sure he didn’t do an encore or anything.
